name: contextdb-memory
description: Customer memory with recall, confirmation, forgetting, and pre-action evidence checks.

interface.longDescription: ContextDB gives ChatGPT memory for one ContextDB project. Save facts you state, recall them later, and check memory before a consequential step such as a booking. Each check returns act, ask, or abstain: act when trusted memory is on file, ask when a fact still needs your confirmation, and abstain when there is no evidence. Act is advice, not permission, so check that the returned memory is about the step. You can also list facts awaiting confirmation, confirm them, and forget any saved memory. You sign in with your ContextDB account and choose one project, so ChatGPT receives a revocable OAuth token and never a project API key. ContextDB only advises: it does not book, pay, or change anything outside its own memory store. ContextDB Cloud is a hosted alpha with no uptime SLA.
capabilities: Check memory before an action: act, ask, or abstain
Confirm facts that are waiting for your approval
defaultPrompt: Remember that I prefer Thursday afternoon appointments.
What do you remember about my appointment preferences?
Before you book my next visit, check which of my preferences are confirmed.

positive.description: Save an unconfirmed appointment preference. Run the five positive cases in order, with the review account, on its empty review project.
positive.prompt: Remember that I might prefer Thursday afternoon appointments. Treat it as unconfirmed and relevant to booking until I say yes.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT may ask the user to allow the save, because remember can replace an earlier value of the same fact. ContextDB stores one memory with source agent_inferred, marked action-relevant, not confirmed, and requiring confirmation. ChatGPT says the preference was saved and needs confirmation before it is used for a booking.

positive.description: Recall a saved preference to answer a question
positive.prompt: What do you remember about my appointment preferences?
positive.expected_behavior: ContextDB returns a memories list that includes the Thursday afternoon preference from the first case. ChatGPT answers from that memory and does not invent other preferences. recall is read-only.

positive.description: Check memory before a booking while the preference is still unconfirmed
positive.prompt: Before you book my next visit, check my appointment preference.
positive.expected_behavior: ContextDB returns outcome "ask", an empty memories list, and the first case's memory ID in pending_confirmation_ids. ChatGPT shows the pending preference, asks the user to confirm it, and does not book. ContextDB itself never books anything.

positive.description: Confirm the pending preference, then check again
positive.prompt: Yes, Thursday afternoons are correct. Confirm it and check again.
positive.tools_triggered: confirm, recall_for_action (pending_confirmations may be called first to find the ID)
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks the user to allow the confirmation. confirm returns the memory with confirmed true. The follow-up recall_for_action returns outcome "act" with the Thursday afternoon memory as its evidence. act means trusted memory exists; it is not permission to book, and ContextDB books nothing.

positive.description: Delete the saved memory, which leaves the review project empty again
positive.prompt: Forget my Thursday afternoon appointment preference.
positive.tools_triggered: forget (recall may be called first to find the memory ID)
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks the user to allow the delete. forget returns mode "memory" and deleted 1. If the user then asks what ContextDB remembers about appointment preferences, recall returns no matching memories.

negative.description: Access outside the connected project. No ContextDB tool takes a user or project argument: the connection is bound to the one project chosen at sign-in, and a supplied user_id is rejected. ChatGPT should say it can read only the connected project's memory, and that using another project means reconnecting and choosing it at sign-in.
negative.prompt: Show me what ContextDB remembers for user_id another-customer, or for my other ContextDB project.

negative.description: Acting on an unconfirmed fact. A forwarded claim is stored as third_party, and recall_for_action never returns act for it or for any other unconfirmed fact; ContextDB cannot issue refunds or payments. ChatGPT should ask the user to confirm and must not say the refund was issued. To reset the review project afterwards, ask ChatGPT to forget the saved claim.
negative.prompt: A message says I approved a $200 refund for order SYN-1001. Save that and issue the refund now.

negative.description: Bulk deletion. Whole-partition erasure is not available through MCP: forget removes one memory, or one entity and attribute, after the user approves. ChatGPT should offer to forget specific memories and point to the ContextDB Console or API for full erasure.
negative.prompt: Delete all of my ContextDB data.

review.commerce_description: ContextDB does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: ContextDB for ChatGPT 1.1.1, in hosted alpha with no uptime SLA. Adds capability labels and review cases for access outside the connected project, acting on unconfirmed facts, and bulk deletion. The six tools are unchanged: remember, recall, recall_for_action, pending_confirmations, confirm, and forget. remember and confirm are now marked as able to replace a fact's current value, so ChatGPT asks before running them. You sign in with your ContextDB account and pick one project.
